newsitem.title: USA: Bombing prosecution expected to rest case Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Bombing prosecution expected to rest case Wednesday.

text.p: The prosecution in the Oklahoma City bombing case is expected to rest its case on Wednesday, the trial judge announced on Tuesday.
Federal Judge Richard Matsch told the court after an 11 minute bench conference: "at some time tomorrow the government will rest its case."
The jury was not in the courtroom when the judge made his announcement at the end of the day's testimony.

Prosecutors have presented more than 130 witnesses in a little more than three weeks who testified about accused bomber Timothy McVeigh's anger toward the U.S. government and his attempts to buy components to make the bomb.
McVeigh, 29, has pleaded not guilty to setting the April 19, 1995 blast at the Alfred P. Murrah building that killed 168 people. If convicted, he faces the death penalty.
When the prosecution finishes it will then be the defense's turn to put on witnesses.
